why: The next unit of each type is always more expensive than the last, so buying the globally cheapest available unit m times is optimal. A min-heap keyed by each type's next price does that: pop the cheapest, then push that type's next price (+ b[i]).
hints: Each type's prices go up as you buy more of it. Is the cheapest unit available right now ever a bad buy?
No: costs per type are increasing, so the m cheapest units overall form a valid purchase. Repeatedly take the smallest current price.
Min-heap of (next price, type). Pop m times, add to the total, push (price + b[i], i). O((n + m) log n).
pitfalls: Item j of type i costs a[i] + (j - 1) * b[i]: the first unit costs exactly a[i].
Total can reach about 10^5 * (10^5 + 10^10); use 64-bit integers outside Python.
Do not pre-generate m units per type (n * m is 10^10).
